content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef, boiled rice and vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens). It is served with a smooth gravy that ties the ingredients together and adds a savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is an excellent source of iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
Rice provides complex carbohydrates that give lasting satiety.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C and glucosinolates, compounds with anti‑cancer properties.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale) contain high amounts of vitamin K and folate.
Gravy is often made from broth and a small amount of flour, giving it a thick, aromatic consistency.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Beef protein helps build and repair muscle tissue.

items.title: Provides steady energy
items.content: Complex carbs from rice supply a stable glucose release.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C from broccoli and leafy greens helps neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Zinc from beef and vitamin A from carrots boost immune function.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Consuming large amounts of beef may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravy often contains salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If the gravy is thickened with wheat flour, it should be avoided by those with celiac disease.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Beef must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot. Garnish with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or soy sauce to taste. Vegetables can be eaten as whole pieces or mashed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For freezing, pack in portion‑size bags and use within 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C.
